messages.content: 請給我過去5年孟加拉和印度的老虎數量規模。同時提供尼泊爾和馬來西亞未來10年老虎數量的預測規模。

function.name: crop_yield_get_history
function.description: Retrieve historical crop yield data of a specific crop in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

years.description: Number of years of history to retrieve.

function.name: animal_population_get_history
function.description: Retrieve historical population size of a specific species in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

years.description: Number of years of history to retrieve.

function.name: animal_population_get_projection
function.description: Predict the future population size of a specific species in a given country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

years.description: Number of years in the future to predict.

The user wants:

- Past 5 years tiger population in Bangladesh and India.
- Future 10 years tiger population in Nepal and Malaysia.

We have two functions:

- animal_population_get_history(country, species, years)
- animal_population_get_projection(country, species, years)

We need to call these functions twice each? Actually we need 4 calls: 2 history calls (Bangladesh, India) and 2 projection calls (Nepa, Malaysia). We can combine them into separate calls or maybe combine into one call per country? The function signature expects a single country, species, years. So we need separate calls for each country.

Thus we will call:

1. animal_population_get_history(country="Bangladesh", species="Tiger", years=5)
2. animal_population_get_history(country="India", species="Tiger", years=5)
3. animal_population_get_projection(country="Nepa", species="Tiger", years=10) but note the country name: "Nepa" is likely "Nepa" but correct is "Nepa"?
